items.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24
items.q: And Mrs. Clara Mare, correspondent secretary.

ctx.x: That's where they all had the mademoiselles. Let me say this is Rio 3, and we're interviewing Mrs. and Mrs. A.C. Senegal, May the 24th, 1862. See, we've seen these pictures of your grandchildren here. We talked about that just on the end of the last Rio. And then you showed me the picture of the boy in the moment here too. Yeah.

Uh-huh. Yeah, she wanted me to say the names of these on this picture? Yeah. This is my granddaughter, Sylvia Serena. She's now Mrs. Webb. And she's the first, she was the first mademoiselle Fiesta. And Barbara Ann, Senegal, granddaughter of Mrs. A.C. Senegal, Mrs. Senegal. And she was a queen when her grandfather was king. She was king, she was a queen. She was king, right? That was nice. That was nice. When he was king, she was his queen. And this is Jocelyn Marie's Romanian. She was maid to her cousin. No, no,…
I wanted to ask you about this postcard. Let's see, we've got on here that you were having a meeting, and you were going to have a block dance Friday, May the 6th, 1960, at 1660 North Miro?
